procedure: All 40 native-BLOCK (N/Bears) target images audited by the agent in two fixed-order contact sheets of 20. Arm identity was constant (all N), so blinding was not applicable; the earlier 20-tile audit WAS arm-blinded. These are AGENT JUDGMENTS, not independent human review.
interpretation: Systematic, one-directional generated-domain scoring failure on the EDITED arm: the frozen presence judge answers 'yes, a bear is visible' on 5/40 native-BLOCK images in which the agent sees no bear. The failure mode is confusion of stylised cartoon quadrupeds (dogs, foxes, cats) and crowded Byzantine/Van Gogh scenes with bears. The 120-photograph COCO controls (20/20 sensitivity and 20/20 specificity per object, including related-animal negatives) did NOT detect this, because real photographs lack that stylisation. This is exactly the limitation the protocol warned of: small real-image controls do not establish synthetic-domain validity. Direction matters: the error is CONSERVATIVE with respect to erasure, over-reporting residual target and therefore UNDER-reporting suppression.
